documents.title: Interim Policy Prohibiting Entering Confidential Information into Generative AI
documents.summary: A short interim IT data-protection policy applying to all WPI students, faculty and staff. It bans entering confidential institutional, employee or student data into generative AI tools, points to a list of authorized tools, and says a fuller policy is being developed. It says nothing about coursework use of AI.
documents.stance_why: The document says 'Do not enter Confidential Information into generative AI tools' and points to 'authorized tools'; it is a narrow ban on one kind of input, not a general AI ban or coursework rule, so it restricts rather than prohibits, and it delegates nothing to instructors.

units.why: Explains the data-exposure risk behind the rule: 'any private or confidential information entered into a generative AI tool is at risk of becoming public'. It is a privacy fact that grounds the policy, so P50 (protect confidential data); informs, not a command.
units.anchor: confidential information entered into a generative AI tool is at risk of becoming public

units.why: States that information entered into a generative AI tool 'immediately becomes part of the generative AI's information database', a claim that tools retain prompts. P50 covers 'AI tools store prompts'.
units.anchor: immediately becomes part of the generative AI's information database
units.frag_start: Members of the WPI community may

units.why: Says the policy is 'interim' while 'a more comprehensive policy is collaboratively developed', so it is provisional and will be replaced. P54 (revisit regularly) fits.
units.anchor: put in place on an interim basis
units.policy: The policy is in place on an interim basis to deal with immediate risks of unintended disclosure of Confidential Information while a more comprehensive policy is collaboratively developed.

units.why: Describes how the policy is being made: WPI has been 'collaboratively reviewing' its Data Classification and Usage Policy and intends to add generative AI language. This is policy-making process (P84); P54 is about provisionality, which the previous unit covers.
units.anchor: we have been collaboratively reviewing WPI's Data Classification and Usage Policy
units.frag_end: related to generative AI usage into that revised policy.
units.policy: WPI is collaboratively reviewing its Data Classification and Usage Policy, last revised in 2019, and intends to integrate language related to generative AI usage into it.
units.fit_note: Also signals a planned revision of an existing data policy to include AI, which is partly P54.

units.why: Sets scope: the policy 'applies to all students, faculty, and staff at WPI', which defines who is bound. P61 covers definitions that set what a policy covers.
units.anchor: This Policy applies to all students, faculty, and staff at WPI.
units.fit_note: Scope of persons covered rather than a definition of AI.

units.why: Defines 'Confidential Information' (institutional, employee, student data not public, such as SSNs, FERPA records) to set what may not be entered. It is a scope definition so P61; it defines the data not AI, hence the fit note.
units.anchor: confidential WPI institutional data, confidential WPI employee data, and WPI student data
units.fit_note: Defines the protected data category rather than AI or AI tools.

units.why: The core rule: 'Do not enter Confidential Information into generative AI tools'. A prohibition on one kind of AI input to protect confidential data; P50 fits best, P49 is narrower and about students uploading course materials.
units.anchor: Do not enter Confidential Information into generative AI tools

units.why: Points users to 'a list of authorized tools' on the ITS knowledgebase, implying use of university-approved tools. P92 (use university-licensed or approved AI tools) fits.
units.anchor: A list of authorized tools can be found on the ITS knowledgebase
units.policy: A list of authorized tools can be found on the ITS knowledgebase or by contacting the ITS Service Desk.
units.fit_note: Only points to the list; does not explicitly require using only authorized tools.

units.why: Tells people with questions to 'seek guidance' from a manager, department head or ITS 'before entering information in a generative AI tool'. That is ask-before-using (P10), here limited to data entry.
units.anchor: you should seek guidance from your manager, Department Head or WPI's Information Technology Services

units.why: Names the policy sponsors (Chief Information Officer; Chief Information Security Officer) and responsible department (Information Technology), so it states who owns the policy. P80 fits.
units.anchor: Policy Sponsor: Chief Information Officer; Chief Information Security Officer
units.policy: Policy sponsor is the Chief Information Officer and Chief Information Security Officer; the responsible department is Information Technology.

units.why: Records presidential approval of the first interim policy (December 4, 2023) and later extensions, describing how and when the policy was adopted. P84 fits; P54 not chosen since this is dated history, not a promise of review.
units.policy: The first interim policy took effect on presidential approval on December 4, 2023, and has been extended through interim periods ending Sept. 26, 2026.

notes: Only one included document; an IT data-protection interim policy with no coursework guidance. School, computing and course layers not coded (none found or deferred).
